integrity.reasoning: Integrity has 1/3 score-eligible evidence layers; missing evidence reduces availability and confidence but is never treated as contradiction. Integrity confidence reflects how many of the three evidence layers were checked. To see how many checks passed, refer to the integrity value and the layer results. Numeric release requires at least 2 populated contributing layer(s) and an assessed qualifying cross-evidence fact (signed_attestation, recorder_metadata); the value is withheld (insufficient_assessed_layers). An ordinary contradiction never releases a value. No qualifying cross-evidence was assessed for this submission. The files and claims have been checked against each other, but this does not guarantee who created the material, when it was recorded or that the recording session took place. Signed origin evidence, where available, is shown in attestation_strength. Structural validity and cryptographic attestation are reported separately and do not raise integrity. Legacy signal comparisons are disabled by policy and do not produce findings or affect integrity.

assessment.reason: No sharp band limit below the Nyquist frequency was found.

limitations: A band limit shows where the decoded audio stops, not who made the file or why.
Mastering with a low-pass filter, band-limited source material (speech, old recordings) or very quiet audio can look the same as a lossy or resampled history.
Thresholds are exploratory and uncalibrated; absence of a band limit does not show a file is original.

calibration.summary: Per-file content band limit from a 90th-percentile spectrum: a sharp cliff (>= 20 dB) or a step into a flat noise floor (>= 6 dB). Thresholds were set on the SoniqTools Bach clip, locally made trick files and six 320 kbps MP3s from a free-music site. Every Lumina music WAV tested is band-limited at 17.4-19.9 kHz by the generator, so a band limit is not evidence of a lossy history.
